rules.reason: The shared 2026 grantseeker policy excludes individuals, government entities and public institutions. DRAF explicitly directs funding information to this sister-fund page; allocation and OPD requirements still need review.

The PAD 2026 call expressly excludes businesses/business associations and schools, colleges or universities. Indigenous leadership, community endorsement and receipt requirements remain manual checks.

The SEED eligibility policy supports organizations, collectives and informal groups, not individuals. Assess a sponsored project using its actual applicant; trans leadership and movement-building requirements remain manual.
The THRIVE eligibility policy supports organizations, collectives and informal groups, not individuals. Prior-grantee status, leadership and budget requirements still need review.
The foundation does not provide direct funding to individuals. Support through separately funded organizations is a different application route.
MCFA expressly does not provide financial support to individuals. Tax status and Americas program scope remain separate checks; US incorporation is not inferred.
The current grantseeker policy excludes support to individuals for any purpose. A qualified project applying through an organizational applicant is assessed using that applicant’s status.
The 2026 infrastructure call expressly says nonprofit organizations cannot apply. Farmer status, farming tenure and eligible states remain necessary manual checks; the round is closed.
Thriving Cultures does not grant directly to individuals; its nonprofit regranting partners may separately support artists. Invitation and project requirements remain manual.
This specific simplified 2026 call supports nonprofit initiatives working throughout Brazil. This necessary country check does not replace its community, legal-form or closed-round restrictions.

Seed 2026 requires direct community benefit in an Ontario catchment area. Canada is only a necessary country condition; Ontario locality, category exceptions and closed-round status still need review.

Drosos excludes projects outside its explicit geography. Germany is limited to eastern Germany, so country fit still requires a subnational check; youth, independence and nonprofit activity requirements remain manual.

The general grant policy excludes grants to individuals. Use the actual applicant, including an organizational fiscal sponsor. UK direct benefit is a separate manual condition, not a strict activity-location rule.

FCA expressly considers only organizations based in these seven countries. Nicaragua additionally requires ability to receive funds in the United States; community leadership and legal-form conditions remain manual.
McConnell expressly requires funded project activities to take place in Canada. CRA qualified/non-qualified donee and entity requirements remain manual; the current portal is closed.
The current Freedom Together policy exclusively supports US-based grantees. This concerns the actual applicant’s base, not the project lead’s citizenship or an inferred registration country.
The official FAQ expressly says Schusterman does not provide grants to individuals. Invitation and portfolio fit remain necessary manual checks.

This specific October 2026 call funds feminist agroecology and community forests in Liberia. General Siemenpuu programs elsewhere are distinct; registration, themes, cofinance and community consent still require review.

TCI’s fellowship applicant and awardee must be a current or past partner host organization. The individual fellow’s eligibility is a separate condition; personal applications cannot substitute for the host.
WKKF expressly cannot make grants to individuals. Use the actual applying organization/sponsor; thematic and Mexico/Haiti subregional fit still require confirmation.

The Benito Massó 2026 call is a scholarship for qualifying students, not an organizational project grant. Afrodescendant identity, Puerto Rico residency, study, progress and financial-need checks remain manual.
The partnership guidance excludes for-profit structures and public institutions. Community leadership, political purpose and other partnership criteria still need manual confirmation.

These regional Charity Pot guidelines support not-for-profit groups and explicitly exclude individuals and profit-making organisations. Use the actual applying group or fiscal sponsor; regional routing and the announced reopening still require confirmation.

The Australian Charity Pot guidelines exclude organisations operating a for-profit model, including social enterprises. Applications are paused; this rule describes the published programme rather than an available award.

The closed 2026 adaptation call requires work with qualifying communities in seven named Brazilian states. State and community requirements remain manual; this is not a country restriction on the separate general iCS programme.
Section 6.5.6 of this closed 2026 research call excludes for-profit entities and their branches. The separate general iCS donation policy has different exceptions and is not covered by this rule.

This ANU-administered award is a scholarship for qualifying engineering students, not an organisational project grant. Citizenship or permanent residence, gender, residential and study requirements remain manual; the displayed application period is historical.
